'''Robert Richard Anstice''' (1813–1853) was an English clergyman and [[mathematician]] who wrote two remarkable papers on [[combinatorics]],<ref>{{smallcaps|Crilly}}, page 488.</ref> published the same year he died in the [[Cambridge and Dublin Mathematical Journal]]. He pioneered the use of [[Primitive root modulo n|primitive roots]] in this field, anticipating the work of [[Eugen Netto]] on [[Steiner triple system|Steiner's triplets]].

Anstice studied at [[Christ Church, Oxford]],<ref>{{smallcaps|Craik}}, page 336.</ref> where he graduated in 1835, receiving a Master's  in 1837. Nothing is known about his life in the next ten years. In 1846, he was ordained priest, and in the following year he became rector of [[Wigginton, Hertfordshire]].<ref>{{smallcaps|O'Connor & Robertson}}, MacTutor History of Mathematics.</ref> He died there in 1853, and is buried, under a cast iron tombstone, in the churchyard at [[St Michael's Church, Madeley]], Shropshire.<ref name=CSMM/>
